vsm2.17:41.1: 41. Now, as regards these two states that are starting points in expositions of the process of becoming,
vsm2.17:41.2: in some instances the Blessed One teaches the Dhamma based on a single one of these states,
vsm2.17:41.3:
for instance, “Accordingly, bhikkhus, formations have ignorance as their cause,
consciousness has formations as its cause” (S II 31), etc.;
vsm2.17:41.4:
likewise, “Bhikkhus, craving increases in one who dwells seeing enjoyment in things
productive of clinging; with craving as condition there is clinging” (S II 84), and so on.
vsm2.17:41.5: In some instances he does so based on both,
vsm2.17:41.6: for instance: “So, bhikkhus, for the fool who is hindered by ignorance and tethered by craving there arises this body.
vsm2.17:41.7: Now, this body with its six internal bases and externally the six bases due to mentality-materiality make a duality.
vsm2.17:41.8:
Due to this duality there is contact, as well as the six pairs of bases, touched through
which the fool feels pleasure and pain” (S II 23f.), and so on.
vsm2.17:42.1:
42. Of these ways of presentation, that cited here in the form “With ignorance as condition
there are formations” should be understood as one based on a single state.
vsm2.17:42.2: This, firstly, is how the exposition should be known “as to different ways of teaching.”
vsm2.17:43.1: 43. 2.As to meaning: as to the meaning of the words “ignorance” and so on.
vsm2.17:43.2:
Bodily misconduct, etc., for example, “ought not to be found” (avindiya), in the sense of being unfit to be carried
out; the meaning is that it should not be permitted.
vsm2.17:43.3: It finds (vindati) what ought not to be found (avindiya), thus it is ignorance (avijjā).
vsm2.17:43.4:
Conversely, good bodily conduct, etc. “ought to be found” (vindiya). It does not find (na
vindati) what ought to be found (vindiya), thus it is ignorance (avijjā).
vsm2.17:43.5:
Also it prevents knowing (avidita) the meaning of collection in the aggregates,
the meaning of actuating in the bases, the meaning of voidness in the elements,
vsm2.17:43.6: the meaning of predominance in the faculties, the meaning of reality in the truths, thus it is ignorance (avijjā).
vsm2.17:43.7:
Also it prevents knowing the meaning of suffering, etc., described in four ways
as “oppression,” etc. (XVI.15), thus it is ignorance.
vsm2.17:43.8:
Through all the kinds of generations, destinies, becoming, stations of consciousness, and abodes of beings in the endless
round of rebirths it drives beings on, thus it is ignorance (avijjā).
vsm2.17:43.9:
Amongst women, men, etc., which are in the ultimate sense non-existent, it hurries on, and amongst the aggregates,
etc., which are existent, it does not hurry on, thus it is ignorance (avijjā).
vsm2.17:43.10:
Furthermore, it is ignorance because it conceals the physical bases and objects of eye-consciousness,
etc., and the dependent origination and dependently-originated states.
vsm2.17:44.1: 44. That due to (paṭicca) which fruit comes (eti) is a condition (paccaya).
vsm2.17:44.2: “Due to” (paṭicca) = “not without that”; the meaning is, not dispensing with it.
vsm2.17:44.4: Furthermore, the meaning of “condition” is the meaning of “help.”
vsm2.17:44.5: It is ignorance and that is a condition, thus it is “ignorance as condition,” whence the phrase “with ignorance as condition.”
vsm2.17:44.6: “They form the formed” (S III 87), thus they are formations.
vsm2.17:44.7:
Furthermore, formations are twofold, namely, (a) formations with ignorance as condition, and (b)
formations given in the texts with the word “formations” (saṅkhāra).
vsm2.17:44.8:
Herein, (a) the three, namely, formations of merit, of demerit, and of the imperturbable, and the three, namely,
the bodily, the verbal, and the mental formations, which make six, are “formations with ignorance as condition.”
vsm2.17:44.9: And all these are simply mundane profitable and unprofitable volition.
vsm2.17:45.1: 45. But (b) these four, namely, (i) the formation consisting of the formed (saṅkhata-saṅkhāra),
vsm2.17:45.2: (ii) the formation consisting of the kamma-formed (abhisaṅkhata-saṅkhāra),
vsm2.17:45.3: (iii) the formation consisting in the act of kamma-forming (forming by kamma—abhisaṅkharaṇa-saṅkhāra),
vsm2.17:45.4:
and (iv) the formation consisting in momentum (payogābhisaṅkhāra), are the kinds of formations
that have come in the texts with the word “formations.”
vsm2.17:46.1:
46. Herein, (i) all states with conditions, given in such passages as “Formations are impermanent”
(S I 158; D II 157), are formations consisting of the formed.
vsm2.17:46.2:
(ii) In the Commentaries material and immaterial states of the three planes generated by kamma
are called formations consisting of the kamma-formed.
vsm2.17:46.3: These are also included in the passage, “Formations are impermanent.”
vsm2.17:46.4: But there is no instance in the texts where they are found separately.
vsm2.17:46.5: (iii) Profitable and unprofitable volition of the three planes is called the formation consisting in the act of kamma-forming.
vsm2.17:46.6: It is found in the texts in such passages as “Bhikkhus, this man in his ignorance forms the formation of merit” (S II 82).
vsm2.17:46.7: (iv) But it is bodily and mental energy that is called the formation consisting in momentum.
vsm2.17:46.8:
This is given in the texts in such passages as “The wheel, having gone as far as the impetus
(abhisaṅkhāra) carried it, stood as though it were fixed” (A I 112).
vsm2.17:47.1: 47. And not only these, but many other kinds of formations are given in the texts with the word “formation” (saṅkhāra),
vsm2.17:47.2:
in the way beginning, “When a bhikkhu is attaining the cessation of perception and feeling, friend Visākha,
first his verbal formation ceases, then his bodily formation, then his mental formation” (M I 302).
vsm2.17:47.3: But there is no formation among them not included by (i) “formations consisting of the formed.”
vsm2.17:48.1:
48. What is said next after this in the rest of the exposition beginning, “With formations as condition,
consciousness” should be understood in the way already stated.
vsm2.17:48.2: But as to those words not yet dealt with: It cognizes (vijānāti), thus it is consciousness (viññāṇa—see M I 292).
vsm2.17:48.3: It bends towards an object (namati), thus it is mentality (nāma).
vsm2.17:48.4: It is molested (ruppati), thus it is materiality (rūpa—see S III 87).
vsm2.17:48.5:
It provides a range for the origins (āye tanoti) and it leads on what is actuated
(āyatañ ca nayati), thus it is a base (āyatana—see XV.4).
vsm2.17:48.6: It touches (phusati), thus it is contact (phassa).
vsm2.17:48.7: It is felt (vedayati), thus it is feeling (vedanā— see M I 293).
vsm2.17:48.8: It frets (or it thirsts—paritassati), thus it is craving (taṇhā).
vsm2.17:48.9: It clings (upādiyati), thus it is clinging (upādāna).
vsm2.17:48.10: It becomes (bhavati) and it makes become (bhāvayati), thus it is becoming (bhava).
vsm2.17:48.11: The act of being born is birth.
vsm2.17:48.12: The act of growing old is ageing.
vsm2.17:48.13: By means of it they die, thus it is death.
vsm2.17:48.14: The act of sorrowing is sorrow.
vsm2.17:48.15: The act of lamenting is lamentation.
vsm2.17:48.16:
It makes beings suffer (dukkhayati), thus it is pain (dukkha); or it consumes in two ways (dvedhā khaṇati—see
IV.100) by means of the two moments (khaṇa) arising and presence, thus it is pain (dukkha).
vsm2.17:48.17: The state of a sad mind (dummana-bhāva) is grief (domanassa).
vsm2.17:49.1: 49. And the words “There is” should be construed with all the terms, not only with those beginning with sorrow;
vsm2.17:49.2: for otherwise, when “With ignorance as condition, formations” was said, it would not be evident what they did,
vsm2.17:49.3:
but by construing it with the words “There is” (or “there are”), since “ignorance
as condition” stands for “it is ignorance and that is a condition,”
vsm2.17:49.4:
consequently the defining of the condition and the conditionally-arisen state
is effected by the words “with ignorance as condition there are formations.”
vsm2.17:50.2: By that he shows that it is with ignorance, etc., as the causes and not with creation by an Overlord, and so on.
vsm2.17:50.5: Mass of suffering: totality of suffering; not a living being, not pleasure, beauty, and so on.
vsm2.17:50.8: This is how the exposition should be known here “as to meaning.”
vsm2.17:51.1: 51. 3. As to character, etc.: as to the characteristics of ignorance, etc.,
vsm2.17:51.2: that is to say, ignorance has the characteristic of unknowing.
vsm2.17:51.6: Formations have the characteristic of forming.
vsm2.17:51.10: Consciousness has the characteristic of cognizing.
vsm2.17:51.11: Its function is to go before (see Dhp 1).
vsm2.17:51.13: Its proximate cause is formations; or its proximate cause is the physical-basis-cum-object.
vsm2.17:51.14: Mentality (nāma) has the characteristic of bending (namana).
vsm2.17:51.16: It is manifested as inseparability of its components, that is, the three aggregates.
vsm2.17:51.18: Materiality (rūpa) has the characteristic of being molested (ruppana).
vsm2.17:51.19: Its function is to be dispersed.
vsm2.17:51.20: It is manifested as morally indeterminate.
vsm2.17:51.22: The sixfold base (saḷāyatana) has the characteristic of actuating (āyatana).
vsm2.17:51.23: Its function is to see, and so on.
vsm2.17:51.24: It is manifested as the state of physical basis and door.
vsm2.17:51.26: Contact has the characteristic of touching.
vsm2.17:51.28: It manifests itself as coincidence of internal and external base and consciousness.
vsm2.17:51.29: Its proximate cause is the sixfold base.
vsm2.17:51.30: Feeling has the characteristic of experiencing.
vsm2.17:51.31: Its function is to exploit the stimulus of the objective field.
vsm2.17:51.32: It is manifested as pleasure and pain.
vsm2.17:51.34: Craving has the characteristic of being a cause that is, of suffering.
vsm2.17:51.38: Clinging has the characteristic of seizing.
vsm2.17:51.39: Its function is not to release.
vsm2.17:51.40: It is manifested as a strong form of craving and as false view.
vsm2.17:51.42: Becoming has the characteristic of being kamma and kamma-result.
vsm2.17:51.43: Its function is to make become and to become.
vsm2.17:51.44: It is manifested as profitable, unprofitable, and indeterminate.
vsm2.17:51.46: The characteristic of birth, etc., should be understood as stated in the Description of the Truths (XVI.32f.).
vsm2.17:51.47: This is how the exposition should be known here “as to character, etc.”
vsm2.17:52.1: 52. 4. As to singlefold, and so on: here ignorance is singlefold as unknowing, unseeing, delusion, and so on.
vsm2.17:52.2: It is twofold as “no theory” and “wrong theory” (cf. §303);
vsm2.17:52.4: It is threefold as associated with the three kinds of feeling.
vsm2.17:52.5: It is fourfold as non-penetration of the four truths.
vsm2.17:52.6: It is fivefold as concealing the danger in the five kinds of destinies.
vsm2.17:52.7:
It should, however, be understood that all the immaterial factors of the dependent origination
have a sixfold nature with respect to the six doors and objects.
vsm2.17:53.1:
53. Formations are singlefold as states subject to cankers (Dhs 3),
states with the nature of result (Dhs 1), and so on (cf. Vibh 62).
vsm2.17:53.2: They are twofold as profitable and unprofitable;
vsm2.17:53.3: likewise as limited and exalted, inferior and medium, with certainty of wrongness and without certainty.
vsm2.17:53.4: They are threefold as the formation of merit and the rest.
vsm2.17:53.5: They are fourfold as leading to the four kinds of generation.
vsm2.17:53.6: They are fivefold as leading to the five kinds of destiny.
vsm2.17:54.1: 54. Consciousness is singlefold as mundane (Dhs 3), resultant (Dhs 1), and so on.
vsm2.17:54.2: It is twofold as with root-cause and without root-cause and so on.
vsm2.17:54.3: It is threefold as included in the three kinds of becoming;
vsm2.17:54.4: as associated with the three kinds of feeling;
vsm2.17:54.5: and as having no root-cause, having two root-causes, and having three root-causes.
vsm2.17:54.6: It is fourfold and fivefold respectively according to generation and destiny.
vsm2.17:55.1: 55. Mentality-materiality is singlefold as dependent on consciousness, and as having kamma as its condition.
vsm2.17:55.2: It is twofold as having an object in the case of mentality, and having no object in the case of materiality.
vsm2.17:55.3: It is threefold as past, and so on.
vsm2.17:55.4: It is fourfold and fivefold respectively according to generation and destiny.
vsm2.17:56.1: 56. The sixfold base is singlefold as the place of origin and meeting.
vsm2.17:56.2: It is twofold as sensitivity of primary elements and as consciousness of the sixth base, and so on.
vsm2.17:56.3: It is threefold as having for its domain objective fields that are contiguous, non-contiguous, and neither (see XIV.46).
vsm2.17:56.4:
It is fourfold and fivefold respectively as included in the kinds of generation and destiny.
The singlefoldness, etc., of contact, etc., should be understood in this way too.
vsm2.17:56.5: This is how the exposition should be known here “as to singlefold and so on.”
vsm2.17:57.1:
57. 5. As to defining of the factors: sorrow, etc., are stated here for the purpose of showing
that the Wheel of Becoming never halts;
vsm2.17:57.2: for they are produced in the fool who is afflicted by ageing and death,
vsm2.17:57.3:
according as it is said: “The untaught ordinary man, bhikkhus, on being touched by painful
bodily feeling, sorrows, grieves and laments,
vsm2.17:57.4: beating his breast, he weeps and becomes distraught” (M III 285; S IV 206).
vsm2.17:57.5:
And as long as these go on occurring so long does ignorance, and so the Wheel of Becoming renews
its revolution: “With ignorance as condition there are formations” and so on.
vsm2.17:57.6:
That is why the factors of the dependent origination should be understood as twelve by taking
those that is, sorrow, etc., along with ageing-and-death as one summarization.
vsm2.17:57.7: This is how the exposition should be known here “as to defining of the factors.”
